name: Computer Science

requirements.label: Introductory programming (C- or higher)
requirements.note: Prerequisite for CS 2100 (C- or higher, or CS 1110 place-out test).

requirements.label: Data Structures and Algorithms 1 (C- or higher)
requirements.note: Current SEAS students changing to or adding the BSCS may do so only after completing CS 2100 with a C- or better. SEAS first-years declare in their second semester (SEAS major declaration deadline March 1) and do not need CS 2100 first.

declaration.notes: SEAS first-years declare a major in their second semester (deadline March 1 per the 2026 orientation deck); students who transfer into SEAS declare on transfer and are placed in their major of choice. Current SEAS students switching to or adding BSCS: CS 2100 with C- or better, then the DocuSign Change of Major / Additional Major Declaration form. College students must apply for internal (intra-university) transfer to SEAS: cumulative GPA > 2.0, good standing, and completed APMA 1090|MATH 1310 (for Fall 2025+ starters), APMA 1110|MATH 1320, APMA 2120|MATH 2310, CHEM 1410|1610|1810 + lab 1411|1611|1811, CS 1110-1113, PHYS 1420|1425|1710 + lab PHYS 1429|2030; application windows Nov 15-Dec 15 (spring entry) and May 1-Jun 1 (fall entry). College students may alternatively pursue the B.A. in Computer Science.

requirements.label: Engineering mathematics
requirements.note: APMA 1090 required for students matriculating Fall 2025 and later (earlier students had 3 more UE credits instead).

requirements.label: Physics I
requirements.note: Equivalents (PHYS 1420/1710, lab 2030) from the SEAS internal-transfer page.

requirements.label: Physics II or Applied Physics
requirements.note: PHYS 2415 + PHYS 2419, or ECE 2200 Applied Physics (the CS example schedule uses ECE 2200).

requirements.label: Engineering foundations
requirements.note: ENGR 1410/1420 are the Rodman Scholars versions.

requirements.label: Science, Technology and Society
requirements.note: STS 4500 in fall of 4th year, STS 4600 in spring of 4th year.

requirements.label: Computer science foundation and required courses
Senior thesis (CS portion)
requirements.note: Option (c) CS 4991 (0 credits) also requires an extra graded 3-credit CS 4000-level course not used for any other CS requirement.

requirements.label: Two APMA electives
requirements.note: APMA 3120 and APMA 3150 cannot both count; STAT 3080 cannot replace APMA 3150; APMA 3110 does not count.

requirements.label: Math and science elective
requirements.note: Any APMA 2000+ course not otherwise required and not duplicative; others by petition.

requirements.label: Computer science electives
requirements.note: '15 credits of CS-mnemonic electives'; uvacsadvising labels CS 3205, 3250, 3501, 3710 and 4000-level courses (incl. CS 4970, 4993) as CS electives. 3000+ range is an approximation.

requirements.label: Humanities and social science electives
requirements.note: 15 HSS credits total (9 from SEAS general requirements + 6 more), from the SEAS approved list chosen with an advisor. Subject list here is an approximation of 'humanities and social sciences' (incl. non-native foreign languages); native-language communication, COMM and SCPS courses do not count; some specific ANTH/ECON/ENSP/GDS/MDST/PSYC/SOC/STS courses are excluded.

requirements.label: Unrestricted electives
requirements.note: Any graded course except math below MATH 1310, duplicative courses, intro programming, and SCPS courses. 15 credits for students who matriculated before Fall 2025.

notes: 126 total credits (sum of checklist categories and the example 8-semester plan). 2.0 GPA in CS courses required to graduate (all attempts count). Prereq grade minimum C- for CS 2100/2120/2130 (intro course), CS 3120, CS 3130, CS 3140, CS 3240, CS 4980. CS 2130 also needs familiarity with a C-like language or concurrent CS 2100. CS 4980 requires BSCS major; CS 4991 for BSCS 4th years with STS 4500 pre/co-req. Engineering and McIntire double majors not allowed. Official Record page (catoid=72 poid=11700) not readable; encoded from uvacsadvising (Fall 2025+ checklist).

name: Science, Technology, and Society

declaration.notes: No formal declaration procedure on the page; contact the STS minor advisor (Prof. MC Forelle). College (CLAS) students must meet with the Director of the Minor before declaring. SEAS minors must be declared before the add deadline of the final term.

requirements.label: Electives (12 credits)
requirements.note: At most 6 of the 12 elective credits from outside E&S (non-STS courses). STS 2500/3500/5500 count only for approved topics (e.g. STS 2500: LEGO Course, Technology and the Frankenstein Myth, Science Technology and Environment, Slavery as a Sociotechnical System, Science & Technology in Popular Culture, Cross-Cultural Engineering, Jefferson Wine & Democracy; STS 3500/5500: Matters of Race in Engineering & Technology). Other courses by petition.

notes: 18 credits (6 required + 12 elective). Cannot be combined with the Technology Ethics minor (students may declare only one; no double-counting between them). SEAS-required STS 2600/4500/4600 are not on the minor's list. Open to College students (they must meet with the Director first).

name: Technology Ethics

declaration.notes: Declaration process not described; contact minor advisors Prof. Bryn Seabrook or Prof. William Davis. Minors must be declared before the add deadline of the final term.

requirements.label: Required courses
requirements.note: SEAS students may double-count STS 2600 (a SEAS degree requirement), making the minor effectively 15 additional credits.

requirements.label: Electives (12 credits)
requirements.note: Up to 6 of the 12 elective credits may come from outside E&S. STS 2500 counts only for approved topics: Ethical Analytics: Using Data for Social Good; STS, Ethics, and the Engineering Grand Challenges; Societal Dimensions of Nanotechnology; Responsible Innovation; Ethics, Science Fiction, and the Future; Technology and the Frankenstein Myth; The LEGO Course; Ethics, Gender, and New Reproductive Technologies. STS 2500 is a repeatable topics course, so several sections may count.

notes: 18 credits (6 required + 12 elective). Cannot be combined with the STS minor (declare only one; no double-counting). Eligibility (SEAS vs College) not stated on the page. The page's elective list is short; other STS electives may be approved by the advisors.

name: Science and Technology Policy

declaration.notes: Declaration process not described; contact coordinator Prof. Rider Foley (rwf6v@virginia.edu). Minors must be declared before the add deadline of the final term.

requirements.label: Science and technology policy course
requirements.note: STS 3020 is the spring course of the Policy Internship Program (DC summer internship).

requirements.label: Approved electives (9 credits)
requirements.note: Nine credits of approved electives 'from fields such as history, philosophy, and planning as well as politics and economics'; the approved list is not published on the page, so this cannot be auto-checked. An older description says students take 'two courses in politics and economics' in addition to the policy course.

notes: 18 credits. Elective list not found (page refers to an unlinked list); encoded as an unchecked 9-credit group. The department overview describes an older structure (politics + economics core courses, a policy course designed for the minor, three electives); the current page lists STS 2101 + STS 3300 + one policy course + 9 elective credits. Eligibility and double-counting rules not stated.

name: Technology and the Environment

declaration.notes: Declaration process not described; contact minor coordinator Teresa Culver. Minors must be declared before the add deadline of the final term.

requirements.label: Emphasis area (3 courses in ONE area)
requirements.note: All three must come from the SAME emphasis area: Environmental Planning and Policy (ARCH 2150|GSVS 2150|COMM 3880, ETP 4010, GDS 3114, GSVS 3110, GSVS 3310, LPPP 2200, PLAC 5720, PLAC 5800, PLAC 5863, PLAN 3060, PLAN 3810, PLAN 3840, PLAN 3860, PLAN 5600, PLAN 5740, PLAP 3160|GSVS 3160, PLAP 4800|ETP 4800, STS 2620, STS 2760, SYS 2620); Technology, the Environment, and Society (ANTH 2260, ANTH 2285, ANTH 3240, ANTH 3340, GSGS 2010, GSGS 3118, GSVS 2210, GSVS 4100, HIEU 3321, HIUS 2061, HIUS 2071, HIUS 3131, HIUS 3161, HIUS 3411, PHS 3620, PLAN 3840, PLAN 3815, SOC 3460, SOC 3470, SOC 3490, STS 2500, STS 2760, SYS 3023); Management and Economics (CE 4110, CE 5035, COMM 4251, COMM 4821, COMM 4822, COMM 5161, EBUS 2830, EBUS 4810, ECON 2010, ECON 3010, ECON 3110, ECON 3430, ECON 4430, ENGR 4880, EVSC 2070, GSGS 3330, STS 2740, SYS 2001, SYS 3034, SYS 3060, SYS 4044, SYS 4050|CE 4050). The 'from' list is the union, so the same-area rule is not enforced.

requirements.label: Sixth course from any list
requirements.note: Six distinct courses total from the lists above (the sixth may also be a course approved by petition to the minor supervisory committee). The other five courses are counted in the groups above.

notes: Six courses (~18 credits; the page gives course counts, not credits). No more than two of the six courses may come from the student's own department (at least four outside the major department). Some courses appear in two emphasis lists (PLAN 3840, STS 2760). Eligibility for College students not stated (interdisciplinary minor). The 'Sixth course' group counts all six courses together.

name: Engineering Business

declaration.notes: Lightweight application (student ID, GPA to confirm good standing, brief statement of interest, acknowledgment the minor can be finished before graduation); windows were October 2024 and February 2025 (likely each fall/spring). Open to all Engineering students and B.A. Computer Science students; no class-year restriction. Courses taken before admission count. Start with EBUS 1800.

requirements.label: Engineering Business Integrated Sequence
requirements.note: Substitutions generally not allowed. Older STS-numbered versions of these courses count.

requirements.label: Electives (two 3-credit courses)
requirements.note: Approved list as of Feb 2025; list may change with instructor availability. 'SYS 2/3054' Systems Case Studies (International) is listed as either number.

notes: 15 credits (9 core + 6 elective). Administered by the EBM Program team in Systems & Information Engineering; the current EBUS-based minor replaced the previous Engineering Business Minor (formerly run jointly with McIntire, with STS 2xxx/3xxx electives). EBUS courses count only as unrestricted electives in SEAS degrees (not HSS); SEAS departmental electives on the list may also count as technical electives. Not open to College students other than BACS majors. Compare McIntire's General Business Minor (COMM 1800 start, 15 credits).
